steps.what: Define document-system test scope and expected lifecycle behaviour
Write a test plan covering the specified document-management behaviours

loop.purpose: Draft a bounded test plan from specified requirements
loop.input: Versioned requirements, existing cases and selected system guidance
loop.output: One plan mapping proposed cases to requirements and expected outcomes
loop.check: Specialist checks that cases test intended access, versioning, retrieval and lifecycle behaviour and that expected results come from requirements rather than generated assumptions
loop.stop: One draft; absent expected behaviour, unsafe destructive tests or invented features return to manual planning
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse existing test templates first; changed requirements may need new case descriptions that fixed field substitution cannot supply

steps.what: Review test-plan adequacy and resolve missing or misleading cases
Execute the checked plan in a controlled test environment and assess outcomes

tasks.design: Use a bounded draft in {DOCS} to adapt existing test plans to specified changes. The specialist independently checks coverage and executes the plan in a {OTHER} test environment; generated expected results do not establish correct records behaviour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changed requirements can require repetitive case writing before substantive review.
tasks.enabler_now: Test-planning assistance can supply a first plan for independent checking.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether the test actually distinguishes compliant from incorrect lifecycle behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist understands the intended records procedure and challenges shallow cases.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass case writing while test scope, adequacy and outcome decisions stay human.

reach.task: Design a fault-sensitive document lifecycle test
reach.learn: Trace expected behaviour to a requirement

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents write test plans and tests; that supports candidate planning assistance but not validation of records obligations.
Model knowledge: document-system lifecycle tests need independently specified expected behaviour and safe test records.

assumptions: Boundary is planning, reviewing and executing controlled tests, excluding production release and formal legal interpretation.

Specialist captures requirement IDs and versions, record types, test roles, expected access and lifecycle outcomes, and affected features in s1's 25 hours. Existing procedure owner supplies authoritative rules; missing expectations return to manual clarification, not generated pass criteria.
Try native test templates and existing cases before model drafting; current system runtime earns no saving.
Destructive lifecycle tests use synthetic records in a controlled environment; all execution time remains in s4.
research_questions: Does a reviewed draft reduce case-writing effort without omitting an intended lifecycle outcome?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and substantive plan review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 and net=6 after four upkeep hours. Range assumes some reusable first-draft case writing; scope, independent review and execution retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor regulatory changes relevant to records

steps.what: Define records-law monitoring scope and authoritative publication sources
Collect new regulatory publications from the specified sources
Assess regulatory notices and determine records-management implications with relevant advisers

tasks.design: Configure source-specific subscriptions or saved searches in {EMAIL} and {DOCS} to collect publications selected by the specialist. The specialist assesses applicability and seeks qualified advice where necessary; a notice collection is not proof of compliance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual revisits to the same publication sources can duplicate retrieval effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing publisher subscriptions and saved searches can collect notices deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding which change applies to a particular record type, jurisdiction and procedure.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises uncertain applicability and frames a precise legal question.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated notice collection while impact assessment remains human.

reach.learn: Identify the affected procedure and unresolved applicability question

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: publisher subscriptions and saved searches can collect notices from selected sources without deciding legal applicability.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring and impact assessment, not implementing changed retention rules or guaranteeing legal compliance. National requirements are confirmed locally.

Specialist produces jurisdiction, record categories, authority or publisher identifiers, exact source endpoints or subscriptions, search terms and review frequency in s1's 25 hours. Publishers produce notice identity, date, title and source content as existing external work. Unavailable sources are marked as gaps and checked manually within upkeep; no model-generated relevant-law flag is assumed.
Test native subscriptions before custom collection; only observed manual revisit and retrieval time may shrink, not publisher runtime or substantive reading.
Current legal consultation is unchanged; any additional adviser work must be measured before extending scope.
research_questions: Does a monitored trial collect the same relevant publications while making missed or unavailable sources visible?

incremental.description: Source checks, subscription maintenance and manual coverage gaps

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 and net=19 after six focal upkeep hours. Range assumes some manual source revisits; applicability assessment and actual reading do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Retrieve, distribute and return repository assets

steps.what: Check the user request and authorise exact assets, versions and recipients
Retrieve the exact electronic asset versions from the repository
Distribute the approved asset package through controlled repository access
Collect returned assets, check revisions and return them to the repository

tasks.design: Configure {DOCS} to retrieve and share only an approved manifest's exact asset versions through controlled access. The specialist still verifies the request and handles returned assets or revision conflicts; a changed package or recipient invalidates distribution approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Retrieval and dispatch may require repeated navigation and manual packaging.
tasks.enabler_now: Native repository checkout and controlled-sharing functions can execute an explicit manifest.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding access and understanding whether a returned asset is complete or a conflicting revision.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist resolves access exceptions and protects the integrity of returned records.
tasks.altitude: Less navigation and packaging while access and version-control judgement remain human.

reach.learn: Explain recipients, permission scope and version binding

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document repositories can retrieve exact versions and apply controlled sharing from explicit asset and recipient identifiers.

assumptions: Boundary is specialist retrieval, distribution and any required return; requester authoring or use and existing asset-owner permissions are outside the denominator and unchanged.

Specialist produces asset IDs, immutable version or hash, recipient identities, permission scope, expiry and return requirement in s1's 25 hours after inspecting current metadata and authority. Missing or ambiguous fields stop retrieval for manual handling. S3 verifies retrieved hashes against the manifest and cannot substitute a newer version.

For return cases the requesting user produces the returned file and explanation after distribution and before s4; this existing user work is unchanged. Specialist's 30 hours retain collection, correspondence, revision checks and check-in, with manual conflict resolution and no inferred approved-return flag.
Test native checkout and sharing before code; savings require actual manual navigation, packaging and dispatch, not existing repository runtime.
unknowns: Current manual retrieval and packaging effort
Asset access authority and return frequency
research_questions: Does a dry-run manifest retrieve and distribute only the approved versions to the approved recipients?

already_counted.description: Request, recipient and exact-version checks or capture
Collection and semantic revision checks on returned assets

incremental.description: Manifest maintenance, failed retrieval and delivery exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact manifest version binding asset hashes, recipients, permission scope, expiry and return requirement approved in s1; changed assets or recipients void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55, gross=45 and net=37 after eight focal upkeep hours. Range assumes partly manual retrieval and packaging; access review and all existing return handling retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review current literature on document-management technologies and techniques
Discuss developments and participate in education, workshops or professional meetings

tasks.design: Protect critical reading and professional participation. Material in {DOCS} supports learning, but faster summaries alone do not establish that the specialist understands a new records technique.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful learning requires examining claims and discussing practical consequences.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technical capability removes the learning obligation.
tasks.still_hard: Separating a tool's advertised feature from a technique suitable for the organisation's records.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist relates new ideas to actual governance and user needs.
tasks.altitude: Professional learning remains part of the role.

reach.task: Discuss the limits of a new management technique
reach.learn: Explain applicability and evidence without repeating vendor claims

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: professional reading and participation depend on active understanding and critical discussion.

assumptions: Boundary is technology and technique learning, excluding regulatory monitoring, event booking and project-specific testing.
No structured learning-complete or suitable-technique flag is presumed; assessment and discussion occur within the retained steps.
Use existing professional resources before adding tools; current runtime is not a new labour saving.
Zero upkeep because no new process or technology is introduced.
research_questions: Which learning activity produces a technique the specialist can explain and critically assess?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. No professional learning or participation time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce first-pass test writing, repeated publication collection and asset packaging while retaining records judgement and version integrity.
reach: Frame precise records questions for compliance advisers
Explain controlled-sharing exceptions to security engineers
role.ambitious_version: A document specialist who provides traceable access and well-tested records procedures with less repeated collection and packaging work.
